recruiting: Runs the 2-year rotational GPS Graduate Program, whose rotations include a Corporate (global functions) cluster and international mobility, plus internships searchable by country (search 'INTERNSHIP' with France selected) on the early-careers portal. Working languages are English and French in France. Corporate roles may be scarcer while European restructuring under FaSTLAne 2030 continues.
tinoAngle: Stellantis is in the middle of a huge strategic turnaround, so your consulting training and international track record (Singapore, Madrid, Australia) fit well with strategy or transformation-office internships at Poissy, and your Spanish is an asset for its Iberian and Latin American operations.

name: Michelin
paris: Most corporate functions, including strategy, are at the Clermont-Ferrand headquarters and global R&D centre; the Paris region has a smaller presence, so expect strategy roles to be in Auvergne.
revenue: €26.0bn sales (FY2025, -1.4% at constant FX); segment operating income about €2.9bn
ownership: Listed on Euronext Paris (CAC 40); partnership limited by shares (SCA), widely held
description: World-leading tyre maker for cars, trucks, aircraft, mining and two-wheelers. Under its 'Michelin in Motion' strategy it is diversifying into polymer composites (conveyor belts, seals, high-tech materials), services and experiences such as the Michelin Guide.
sectors: Automotive
Tyres
Materials
Mobility services
health: Sales slipped in 2025 because of weak original-equipment and truck demand and low plant utilisation. H1 2026 was steadier (sales €12.7bn, margin 11.4%, guidance confirmed), but restructuring continues: a US BFGoodrich plant wind-down and a voluntary plan of up to 1,500 positions in France over three years, announced in May 2026. A Capital Markets Day is set for May 2027.

news.title: Michelin H1 2026: margin up to 11.4%, guidance confirmed, three composite acquisitions completed
Michelin plans voluntary workforce adaptation of up to 1,500 positions in France
Michelin reports €26.0bn 2025 sales amid OE and utilisation headwinds

recruiting: Offers internships and work-study placements, plus international graduate programmes: Marketing & Sales (3 positions over 5 years) and Manufacturing (2 positions over 3 years). Offers are posted on recrutement.michelin.fr, and French plus fluent English is expected for roles in Clermont-Ferrand.
tinoAngle: Your AFOCO project on valorising industrial ash fits neatly with Michelin's push into sustainable materials and circularity, which makes a strong hook for a strategy, innovation or sustainable-mobility internship, if you are open to working in Clermont-Ferrand.

name: Valeo
paris: Group headquarters, including corporate strategy, are in Paris, and the group has major R&D and business-group sites across Île-de-France.
ownership: Listed on Euronext Paris; widely held
description: Global automotive supplier focused on electrification (high-voltage powertrain systems, thermal management), driver assistance and software-defined vehicles (sensors, cameras, lidar), lighting and the aftermarket. It operates 149 plants and 59 R&D centres in 29 countries.
sectors: Automotive
Electrification
ADAS
Software-defined vehicles
health: Steady recovery: in 2025 the operating margin reached 4.7%, free cash flow before restructuring hit a record €756m and order intake jumped 38% to €24.6bn. H1 2026 margin rose to 5.0% with guidance reaffirmed, as the Elevate 2028 plan and a €400m European restructuring programme progress.

news.title: Valeo H1 2026: operating margin 5.0%, free cash flow up, 2026 targets reaffirmed
Valeo FY2025: net profit +23%, record order intake up 38%
Net profit up 23%, orders up 38%: Valeo's 2025 shows resilience

recruiting: Recruits interns, apprentices and VIEs (it runs an international VIE programme) through its job-offer portal on valeo.com and through JobTeaser. Corporate strategy and business-group strategy roles sit in Paris. English is the working language, with French useful at headquarters.
tinoAngle: Valeo's strategy agenda (electrification, ADAS, software-defined vehicles, new markets like drones and energy storage) suits your strategy-consulting profile, and its Paris headquarters plus VIE programme give you both a Paris-first option and an international one.

name: Forvia
paris: Group headquarters, including corporate strategy, M&A and the IGNITE transformation teams, are in Nanterre, just west of Paris.
founded: 1997 as Faurecia; became Forvia in 2022 after acquiring Hella
employees: Over 150,000 (2025, before the Interiors sale, which covers about 31,000 people)
revenue: €26.2bn sales (FY2025, flat at constant currency); net loss of €2.1bn after one-off charges
ownership: Listed on Euronext Paris; widely held
description: One of the world's largest automotive suppliers, covering seating, electronics, lighting (via Hella), clean mobility and lifecycle solutions. It is reshaping its portfolio around a 'Growth' cluster (Seating, Electronics) and a 'Value' cluster.
sectors: Automotive
Electronics
Seating
Lighting
health: Deleveraging is the priority: in 2025 the operating margin rose to 5.6% and net debt fell to €6.0bn (1.7x EBITDA), but the net loss was €2.1bn after impairments and no dividend was paid. In April 2026 it agreed to sell Interiors to Apollo funds (€1.82bn enterprise value, closing expected end-2026). The EU-FORWARD plan had announced 6,400 job cuts by end-2025, and H1 2026 confirmed guidance of a 6.0–6.5% margin.

news.title: Forvia H1 2026: margin up to 6.0%, net cash flow +19%, guidance confirmed under IGNITE roadmap
Forvia agrees €1.82bn sale of Interiors business to Apollo funds
Forvia 2025 annual results: higher margin, lower debt, €2.1bn net loss

recruiting: Posts internships (typically 4–6 months), apprenticeships and VIE assignments on its careers site and on JobTeaser, with HQ roles in Nanterre. English is the group language, and French is needed for most French sites.
tinoAngle: Forvia is in the middle of a portfolio transformation (disposals, IGNITE roadmap, cost restructuring), which is exactly the work a strategy-consulting graduate supports, so look for strategy, M&A or transformation internships at the Nanterre HQ, which is easy to reach from Paris.

name: Airbus
hq: Leiden, Netherlands (registered); operational headquarters in Blagnac/Toulouse, France
paris: Corporate Strategy sits in Blagnac (Toulouse); the Paris region hosts Airbus offices and the Élancourt (Defence and Space) and Paris Le Bourget sites.
ownership: Listed on Euronext Paris, Frankfurt and Madrid; France and Germany each hold about 11% and Spain about 4%
description: World's largest commercial aircraft maker (A220, A320neo family, A330neo, A350), with helicopter and defence and space divisions. It delivered 793 commercial aircraft in 2025 and has a backlog of over 9,000.
sectors: Aerospace
Defence
Space
health: Healthy growth: 2025 revenues rose 6% to €73.4bn and adjusted EBIT reached €7.1bn. H1 2026 revenues were up 12% with unchanged guidance (about 870 deliveries, €7.5bn adjusted EBIT), and the group aims for over 1,100 deliveries a year by 2029. Supply-chain strain and the integration of Spirit AeroSystems work packages remain the key risks.

news.title: Airbus H1 2026: revenues +12%, 351 deliveries, 2026 guidance maintained
Airbus targets more than 1,100 annual deliveries by 2029
Airbus reports FY2025: revenues €73.4bn, 793 deliveries

recruiting: Internships in France last 4–6 months; applications open September to December, with summer internships opening in January. The process is an online application, then a video interview, then an interview with the manager. Corporate Strategy posts dedicated end-of-studies internships, such as the 6-month 'Stage 2027 – Stratégie d'Entreprise' in Blagnac starting around March–April 2027, which requires security clearance. EU nationality or French work authorisation is required, and both French and English are used.
tinoAngle: Your international profile (Singapore, Madrid, Australia, three languages) matches Airbus's very multinational culture, and its Corporate Strategy team in Blagnac recruits end-of-studies interns for 2027, so watch for those postings from September through December.

name: Safran
paris: Group headquarters functions, including Strategy and M&A (for example a 'Manager M&A / analyse stratégique' role in Malakoff), are in Paris and the inner suburbs, and many subsidiaries have sites across Île-de-France.
revenue: €31.3bn adjusted revenue (FY2025, +14.7%); recurring operating income €5.2bn (16.6% margin)
ownership: Listed on Euronext Paris (CAC 40); the French State is the largest shareholder
description: Leading aerospace and defence group: through CFM International (with GE) it co-produces the LEAP engine for the A320neo and 737 MAX, and it also makes landing gear, nacelles, aircraft equipment, defence electronics and aircraft interiors.
sectors: Aerospace
Defence
Propulsion
Aircraft equipment
health: Excellent momentum: in 2025 revenue rose about 15% and margin improved by 150bp, with 2028 ambitions raised (about €21bn cumulative FCF over 2024–28). H1 2026 delivered a record 18.4% margin and full-year guidance was raised again. Portfolio moves continue, including the sale of Safran Passenger Innovations and the joint Aubert & Duval stake purchase with Airbus.

news.title: Safran H1 2026: record 18.4% margin, full-year guidance raised
Safran reports strong Q1 2026 with 'little to no impact' from war
Safran reports excellent 2025 and raises its 2028 ambitions

recruiting: Safran plans more than 18,000 hires worldwide in 2026 and lists 4,000+ openings, including internships (stage), apprenticeships and VIE, filterable by contract and country on safran-group.com. Strategy/M&A openings appear at the Paris-area headquarters. French is generally required for French-based roles, alongside English.
tinoAngle: Safran's active M&A and portfolio management (disposals, joint acquisitions with Airbus) is a direct fit for your strategy-consulting Master, so target 2027 end-of-studies internships in the group Strategy/M&A team in the Paris area.

name: Bpifrance
paris: Headquarters and national teams (investment, innovation, strategy) are in Maisons-Alfort and Paris, where Le Hub (the start-up / large-corporate open-innovation unit) is also based; there are 50 regional offices in total.
founded: 2012–2013 (merger of OSEO, CDC Entreprises and FSI)
revenue: €72bn mobilised for companies in 2025 (record), including about €21bn of loans, €2.5bn invested in equity and €30bn+ of export guarantees; net banking income €1.8bn, net income €501m, equity about €30bn (2025)
ownership: Public: owned by the French State (via EPIC Bpifrance) and Caisse des Dépôts
description: France's public investment bank, which finances and invests in companies from start-ups to large caps through loans, guarantees, innovation aid, equity, export insurance and advisory services. Le Hub, launched in 2015, connects start-ups with large corporates for commercial partnerships and open innovation.
sectors: Public finance
Venture capital and private equity
Innovation
Banking
health: Activity hit a record in 2025 (€72bn mobilised), but net income fell about 44% to €501m because of lower dividends and weaker contributions from listed holdings (Stellantis, STMicroelectronics, Soitec). Its 2026–2030 strategy (October 2025) targets €35bn for reindustrialisation, €35bn for climate and €10bn for AI.

news.title: Bpifrance opens H1 2027 internship campaign with nearly 280 offers across France
Bpifrance: record activity in 2025 but net profit down 44%
Bpifrance unveils its 2030 strategy: reindustrialisation, climate, deeptech and AI

recruiting: Runs a 'Jeunes Talents' programme: the campaign for H1 2027 internships (typically 5–6 months) opened on 14 September 2026 with about 280 offers in finance, investment, innovation, digital, data and risk. The process is a CV screen, then an HR phone interview, then an operational interview that may include a case study. Roles are French-speaking.
tinoAngle: An innovation-strategy or Le Hub internship would let you use your consulting skills on start-up/corporate partnerships and industrial or climate projects like your AFOCO ash-valorisation work, and since the H1 2027 campaign opened in September 2026 you should apply now.

name: LVMH
paris: Group holding, including corporate strategy, finance and M&A teams, sits in Paris 8th, with many Maisons (Louis Vuitton, Dior, Sephora) also headquartered in Paris.
ownership: Listed on Euronext Paris (CAC 40); controlled by the Arnault family
description: World leader in luxury goods with 75+ Maisons across fashion and leather goods, wines and spirits, perfumes and cosmetics, watches and jewellery, and selective retailing (Sephora, DFS). The holding steers portfolio strategy, capital allocation and talent across the Maisons.
sectors: Luxury goods, fashion & leather goods, wines & spirits, beauty, watches & jewellery, selective retail
health: 2025 revenue fell 1% organically to €80.8bn with recurring operating profit down 9% to €17.8bn; growth resumed modestly in 2026 (+2% organic over 9M, Q3 +1%), led by jewellery and Sephora while fashion slowed in China. Portfolio pruning continued in 2026 with the sale of Marc Jacobs and most DFS businesses.

news.title: LVMH posts +1% organic growth in Q3 2026, 9M revenue €57.1bn
Q3 organic growth slows amid China downturn (FashionUnited)
H1 2026: €38.6bn revenue, growth accelerates in Q2; Marc Jacobs sale agreed
FY2025 results: €80.8bn revenue, 22% operating margin

recruiting: LVMH holding posts 6-month internships in Paris with January/March 2027 starts (e.g. strategic projects, e-commerce, legal) on its job board, and Maisons recruit separately. Graduate track: LVMH SPRING Future Leaders (3 x 10-month rotations in 3 Maisons), plus SPRING Product Leaders and HR; VIE roles are posted by Maisons abroad.
tinoAngle: Sephora already presented at your Strategy Club, so use that contact to target Sephora's strategy/transformation team or holding-level strategy internships for January 2027, and pitch your Singapore and Madrid experience for an international Maison.

name: Kering
paris: Corporate headquarters, including group strategy, finance and sustainability teams, is in Paris 7th; Saint Laurent and Balenciaga are also Paris-based.
ownership: Listed on Euronext Paris (CAC 40); controlled by the Pinault family via Artémis
description: Global luxury group owning Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta, Balenciaga, Alexander McQueen, Boucheron and Kering Eyewear. Since 2025 CEO Luca de Meo has run a turnaround focused on brand desirability, cost discipline and debt reduction.
sectors: Luxury fashion & leather goods, jewellery, eyewear
health: 2025 revenue fell 10% comparable to €14.7bn with recurring operating income down 33%; H1 2026 returned to slight growth (+1% comparable) and net debt fell from €8.0bn to €3.3bn. Key moves: Kering Beauté sold to L'Oréal (closed March 2026), ReconKering plan unveiled at the April 2026 Capital Markets Day, and a 50-year Gucci beauty licence with L'Oréal.

news.title: H1 2026: back to growth, net debt cut to €3.3bn
How Luca de Meo's financial overhaul gives Kering breathing room (FashionUnited)
Kering grants L'Oréal a 50-year exclusive Gucci beauty licence
FY2025 results: revenue down 10% comparable, CMD announced

recruiting: Kering corporate posts internships (stage) and apprenticeships in Paris across finance, real estate, sustainability and HR, typically 6 months with September or January starts; brands recruit separately. Openings are listed on Kering's talent site and relayed on job boards.
tinoAngle: Kering's turnaround (ReconKering, divestments, store closures) is a live strategy case, and your AFOCO ash-valorisation project gives you a concrete CSR story for its corporate strategy and sustainability teams in Paris.

name: Hermès
hq: Paris, France (rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, 8th arr.)
paris: Head office is on rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, with large corporate and métier teams in Pantin (Greater Paris), where many internships are based.
ownership: Listed on Euronext Paris (CAC 40); majority-controlled by the Hermès founding family
description: Family-controlled French luxury house known for leather goods and saddlery, silk, ready-to-wear, perfume and watches, made largely in its own French workshops. It favours scarcity, craftsmanship and vertical integration over volume.
sectors: Luxury leather goods, fashion, silk & textiles, perfume & beauty, watches
health: 2025 revenue rose 8.9% at constant rates to €16.0bn with a 41% recurring operating margin; H1 2026 grew 6.1% at constant rates to €8.16bn, margin still 41%. It keeps adding leather workshops in France (25th opened 2026) and raised prices about 5-6% in 2026.

news.title: H1 2026 revenue €8.2bn, operating margin holds at 41%
Hermès raises prices about 6% in 2026 (Merca2)
FY2025 results: €16.0bn revenue, +8.9% at constant rates

recruiting: Hermès posts many 4-6 month internships ("STAGE") in Paris and Pantin across marketing, merchandising, finance, ERP and project roles, plus apprenticeships; corporate strategy openings are rare. Selection is highly competitive.
tinoAngle: Hermès is very selective, so lead with your Singapore internship and Asia exposure (Asia ex-Japan is its largest region) and target a business-analysis or project internship in Paris/Pantin as an entry point rather than waiting for a pure strategy title.

name: Chanel
hq: London, UK (global HQ); main French operations in Neuilly-sur-Seine and Paris
paris: Fashion, Watches & Fine Jewellery and Fragrance & Beauty teams sit in Paris and Neuilly-sur-Seine, where Chanel Europe corporate internships (finance, legal, strategy-adjacent) are based.
ownership: Private; controlled by the Wertheimer family
description: Privately held French luxury house active in haute couture, ready-to-wear, leather goods, fragrance and beauty, watches and fine jewellery. CEO Leena Nair leads a strategy centred on creativity (artistic director Matthieu Blazy), manufacturing control and boutiques.
sectors: Luxury fashion, fragrance & beauty, watches & fine jewellery
health: After a 2024 decline, 2025 revenue returned to growth (+2% comparable to $19.3bn) with operating profit around $4.7bn, driven by the Americas while Asia-Pacific dipped slightly. Chanel keeps investing in its supply chain (e.g. 20% stake in an Italian manufacturer) and opened 41 boutiques in 2025, with about 30 planned for 2026.

news.title: Chanel revenue rebounds to $19.3bn as Matthieu Blazy fuels demand
Chanel bounces back in 2025 with 3% growth (Modaes)
Chanel returns to growth as Blazy's designs win over new shoppers

recruiting: Chanel Europe posts many internships for January 2027 starts in Paris and Neuilly (e.g. talent acquisition, sustainability, CRM, pricing analysis, controlling), usually 6 months. Roles titled 'strategy' are rare; business analyst and pricing roles are the closest.
tinoAngle: Chanel suits your Paris-plus-Singapore plan: aim for a business-analysis or pricing internship in Paris now and use your Singapore internship to later target its Asia-Pacific teams in Singapore.

name: L'Oréal
paris: Global headquarters in Clichy, just outside Paris, hosts group strategy, finance and Beauty Tech teams, with R&I in Saint-Ouen and Aulnay.
ownership: Listed on Euronext Paris (CAC 40); Bettencourt Meyers family and Nestlé are the main shareholders
description: World's largest beauty company with brands across consumer products, luxury (Lancôme, YSL Beauty, now Creed), dermatological beauty and professional products. It positions itself as a 'Beauty Tech' leader, with e-commerce above 30% of sales.
sectors: Beauty & cosmetics, luxury beauty, dermocosmetics, beauty tech
health: 2025 sales rose 4.0% like-for-like to €44.05bn with a 20.2% operating margin; H1 2026 accelerated to +6.8% like-for-like with a record 21.3% margin. Strategic moves include integrating Kering Beauté (from April 2026), a 50-year Gucci beauty licence, a Galderma stake raised to 20%, and an AI partnership with OpenAI.

news.title: L'Oréal Groupe and Paris Saint-Germain team up
H1 2026: +6.8% like-for-like, record 21.3% margin
50-year exclusive worldwide licence for Gucci beauty
L'Oréal and OpenAI join forces to transform beauty with AI

recruiting: L'Oréal calls internships and apprenticeships its 'n°1 route' to a job, with 6-month internships (January, July, September starts) in Clichy and the divisions. Graduates can join the SeedZ Management Trainee Programme (permanent hire); VIE roles exist in subsidiaries abroad.
tinoAngle: Your interest in strategy and digital transformation maps directly onto L'Oréal's Beauty Tech push and its Kering Beauté integration, so target strategy or transformation internships in Clichy and mention SeedZ as your graduate route.

name: Accor
paris: Global headquarters is in Issy-les-Moulineaux, where central strategy, development, brand and finance teams (including the Luxury & Lifestyle development office) sit.
ownership: Listed on Euronext Paris (CAC 40); widely held
description: Europe's largest hotel group, operating and franchising 5,800+ hotels and 45+ brands (from ibis and Novotel to Sofitel, Raffles and Ennismore lifestyle brands) in 110+ countries. It runs an asset-light model built on management and franchise fees.
sectors: Hospitality, hotels, lifestyle brands, loyalty
health: 2025 was a record year (RevPAR +4.2%, recurring EBITDA +13.3% to €1.2bn); H1 2026 RevPAR growth slowed to +2.2% due to the Middle East conflict, yet EBITDA still rose 6.5% at constant currency. In July 2026 it agreed to sell its ~30.7% Essendi stake for up to ~€975m and keeps buying back shares.

news.title: H1 2026 results: Accor shows agility; Essendi stake sale agreed
First-half performance dampened by Middle East turmoil (HOTELS)
FY2025 results: record recurring EBITDA of €1.2bn

recruiting: Accor lists hundreds of internships and apprenticeships at its HQ and hotels, plus a Graduate Program track; HQ roles include strategy-type internships such as 'Strategy Analyst Luxury & Lifestyle' and 'Sustainability Strategy & Transformation' in Paris/Issy. Internships are typically 6 months.
tinoAngle: Accor already spoke at your Strategy Club and your six months in Australian hospitality give you real operational credibility, so apply to HQ strategy internships like the Luxury & Lifestyle strategy analyst role in Issy.

name: Decathlon
paris: Corporate and strategy teams sit mainly in Villeneuve-d'Ascq and Lille; Paris hosts flagship stores and some regional teams rather than group strategy.
ownership: Private; controlled by the Mulliez family, with about half of employees as shareholders (2025)
description: World's largest sporting goods retailer, designing its own brands and selling through 1,900+ stores in 80+ territories and online. It is shifting to a 'sport platform' model including marketplace, rental, repair and second-hand.
sectors: Sporting goods retail, product design & manufacturing, e-commerce, circular economy
health: 2025 revenue grew to €16.8bn (+5.6% at constant rates) with net profit up 16% to €910m; about three quarters of sales are outside France. In 2026 it accelerated franchising (master franchisees in ~20 territories) and set a goal of reaching 2 billion people by 2035.

news.title: Decathlon franchises mountain stores and accelerates internationally (L'Express Franchise)
Behind €20.7bn: Decathlon's shift to a sport platform model (Ecommerce Nation)
Decathlon 2025 annual results: revenue €16.8bn, net profit €910m

recruiting: Decathlon offers retail management internships and CDIs nationwide plus HQ internships and apprenticeships in Lille/Villeneuve-d'Ascq (finance, portfolio, marketing ops); international roles exist across 80+ territories. HQ processes typically run 2-4 interview rounds, and practising a sport is valued.
tinoAngle: Decathlon's international expansion and franchise push match your interest in sport and innovation, and your Madrid sales and import/export experience suit an HQ finance/portfolio or international development internship in Lille.

name: Arkopharma
paris: No significant Paris strategy team: management, marketing and production are based in Carros near Nice, with group strategy influenced by parent Dermapharm in Germany.
ownership: Private; subsidiary of Germany's Dermapharm Holding SE (acquired 2022)
description: French leader in herbal medicines and phytotherapy food supplements (Arkogélules), sold mainly in pharmacies, with subsidiaries in seven countries and distribution in 60+ countries. A mid-sized company where strategy work is close to top management.
sectors: Food supplements, phytotherapy, consumer healthcare, pharmacy
health: Arkopharma is undergoing a business-model reorganisation: Dermapharm's segment that includes it was flat in 2025 (€352m) and in H1 2026 (€177m), with restructuring costs at Arkopharma. Dermapharm expects a strong H2 2026 and higher market share and earnings from Arkopharma.

news.title: Dermapharm H1 2026: profitable growth, 'strong second half' expected for Arkopharma
Dermapharm performs in line in Q1 2026 and confirms guidance
Dermapharm FY2025: Arkopharma reorganisation weighs on segment

recruiting: Arkopharma posts 6-month internships and apprenticeships (e.g. marketing product assistant, scientific affairs) at Carros, with October 2026 postings for 2027; spontaneous applications go through a Jobaffinity form. No formal graduate programme or strategy internship track was found.
tinoAngle: You are already working on Arkopharma's growth strategy in your course, so turn that work into a short pitch to management and propose an end-of-studies internship on its turnaround and international growth, where a mid-sized firm gives you more direct impact.
